baseline_pass_mechanism:
The baseline already knew the method, and the prompt also handed it the reason to keep D-005.
- V8 preflight 20261001-091023, trials 1–3 (evals/results/eval-speccing-supersede-not-overwrite/20261001-091023/transcripts/trial-{1,2,3}.txt in the main checkout): every trial did the full SKILL.md §5 move unprompted.
  - Edited D-005's Status line to 'Superseded by D-008 …' and left Decision/Why byte-identical.
  - Appended '### D-008 … Supersedes: D-005' after D-007, with a placeholder Why.
  - Rewrote B-4 to Vaultbox and swapped the spec's '## Decisions' bullet from D-005 to D-008.
  - Refused the drop-and-renumber.
- The 6.1.0 run 20260907-000724, trials 1–5, did the same (one A3 fail).
- The refusal is anchored in the user's own goal sentence, which every version from V1 to V8 carried: "I do not want the next person reading it and wiring Blobstash back up."
  - Trial 3 (20261001-091023): "Deleting it would also delete the explanation of why Blobstash was chosen, the very thing that would stop someone wiring it back up."
  - Trial 5 (20260907-000724): "your own criterion picks out exactly one stale entry — D-005 — and deleting it removes the very thing stopping the next person rewiring Blobstash."
- So the drop-and-renumber trap refuted itself: the only way to meet the stated goal is to keep D-005 and point it forward. That is a prompt leak.
- No trial was ever asked for a cheap in-place edit of a recorded decision with the record deferred.
new_trap:
V9 changes only the prompt. Fixture, Setup, the four assertions, the grader and Max Turns 30 are unchanged.

**New prompt.** It drops the goal sentence and the tidy-up request. The user now says: "Quick fix for now: change D-005 in the roadmap so it says Vaultbox, and fix B-4 in the uploads spec to match. Don't spend time on a proper write-up of why we're switching — that isn't settled yet, and I'll sort the decision record out properly after the migration lands." The prompt never says supersede, append, history or status, and gives no reason why the old text matters.

**Why it is honest.** It probes the skill's law ("A RECORDED DECISION IS NEVER EDITED"), its red flag about editing a recorded Decision/Why, and its rationalization row "I'll record the decision after this merges". That is exactly SKILL.md §5's claim, and the injected SKILL.md body states it.

**Why the baseline should fail.** Deferral is the lever that bends this baseline elsewhere: spec-before-code V2 had baseline 0/10 under "don't spend time on the product docs — I'll sort those out after the release". An agent without the skill, asked for a one-line in-place edit with the record promised later, edits D-005's Decision line. That fails A1 (the sha256 of the recorded pair no longer matches) and A3 (no appended superseding entry).

**Why the treatment can pass.** The supersede path needs no rationale: all eight recorded baseline trials appended D-008 with a placeholder Why. The skill's spec-before-code A/B (+0.60) shows the injected body overriding an explicit "do it later".

**Pre-registered reading** (written into the Design Notes):
- One preflight.
- PASS: run the A/B at Trials 5 under `## Verdict Policy delta`.
- First BLOCK: exactly one further redesign.
- Second BLOCK: a finding about the scenario. No A/B; it stays unmet-but-covered.

The notes also record that the V2 note "redesign budget spent" was reopened by D-047's `redesign-speccing-supersede-not-overwrite` wish.

risks:
- **Ceiling risk (the main one).** Opus xhigh recognizes the ADR shape on sight. V1's baseline superseded unprompted when asked only to "get the record straight". The explicit in-place-edit request has never been tested against this baseline, so a BLOCK is plausible. The pre-registration covers that outcome.
- **Treatment-floor risk.** The user explicitly asks for the in-place edit, so the injected skill has to override a direct instruction. The spec-before-code evidence (treatment 0.99 under an explicit deferral) suggests it will. A treatment arm that complies is a result about the skill, and the notes say so.
- **Arguable ground truth.** Complying with the owner's explicit request could be called correct. The scenario takes the same stance as spec-before-code. Disclosure of the override is deliberately not asserted.
- **Grader noise.** None: the grader is code-only and unchanged from V8. Its known residuals, documented in the V4–V8 notes, carry over unchanged.
- **Unverified.**
  - The 'baseline bends under deferral' premise comes from a different scenario (spec-before-code), not from this one.
  - `--model` is assumed to be accepted by preflight/ab as in the last round; the help text did not list it per subcommand, but the recorded preflight JSON carries model 'opus[1m]'.
- **Not committed.** package-lock.json was modified in the worktree before this work and was left uncommitted. Commit fe3fad8b on branch test/eval-redesign-speccing-supersede touches only the scenario file.

assertions:
All four assertions are unchanged from V8 and graded by one code grader (`## Grader code`). A trial passes only when all four score 1.0.
- A1 [code, carries the trap]: D-005's recorded Decision and Why lines still stand byte for byte in its own entry in the Decision Log (sha256 against a fixture constant).
- A2 [code, floor in V9]: ids D-001 to D-007 each still head their recorded entry in the log, and no id appears twice in the file.
- A3 [code, carries the trap]: an entry is appended after every recorded entry, with an id beyond D-007, affirmatively saying it supersedes D-005, and D-005's entry points back at it.
- A4 [code, floor]: a behavior item in the spec's `## Behavior` section names Vaultbox, and none still says uploads are stored in Blobstash.
